pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and a default of normal. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts the exact list entries: '— high' and '— low' labels, none on normal.
'AC-3' test checks the high, low and normal filters with id order.
'AC-4' test checks the unfiltered list in id order.
'AC-5' test checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses a Set with has().

'AC-7' test asserts exact messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views for an empty table. The 'No match' state test was later weakened (see findings), but AC-7 still covers the behaviour.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high. The 'AC-8' test asserts it, and the config check now accepts a query.

findings.what:
Commit d35426a ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null when there is no

, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The state-table row 'No match' now has no real check of its message. AC-7's own test covers the text, but this is still a weakened test with no justification in the spec.

The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. That is false: the final commit loosened the 'No match' assertion in test/priority.test.js to toBeDefined(). The commit message 'Follow-up edits' also hides this.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or disclose the loosening and give a reason. Use a descriptive commit message.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec and the owner's go. The only addition beyond the ask is the traffic-config query allowance, which is needed for AC-8 and is disclosed.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each is named by a test. All four state rows have a test, but the 'No match' row's message check was weakened in the last commit.
The tests are mostly strong, with exact assertions. The 'No match' state test was loosened to an assertion that cannot fail. I did not run the tests (CI runs them).
The README mentions the priority filter. It does not mention the nav or labels, which is minor.
Validation is correct and the SQL is parameterised. An empty-string priority value returns 400. The empty-versus-no-match logic is correct.
The priority value is whitelisted and bound as a SQL parameter. Titles are HTML-escaped. The nav links are built only from constants. No instructions were planted in the repo content.
The diff changes only a server-rendered HTML string; it touches no template, CSS or UI component files. Only a plain nav line was added.
No browser or UI flow is available. The page is checked by HTML-string tests.
The PR's claim that no tests were loosened is false (see findings). The other claims check out.
